evidence.support_text: The sensitization potential of MIT (99.8% a.i.) was evaluated using the Buehler method with induction doses of 0, 1000, 5000, 15000, or 30000 ppm in distilled water applied on shaved intact flank skin of Hartley guinea pigs. The authors concluded that MIT is a sensitizer at concentrations greater than or equal to 1000 ppm.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Guinea pigs; induction of arsphenamine hypersensitiveness
evidence.support_text: Frei in a series of experiments inducing arsphenamine hypersensitiveness in guinea pigs found that the skin hypersensitiveness was directed toward the aromatic arsenicals in general and that vitamin A had no enhancing effect.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Species: guinea pig
evidence.support_text: In guinea pig sensitization studies on read-across material isobornyl acetate, no reactions indicative of sensitization were observed (RIFM, 2007; Klecak, 1985, 1979). Read-across is used to conclude that isobornyl 2-methylpropionate does not present a concern for skin sensitization.
